$comment: Ownership map: agent type -> globs that agent type may Edit/Write.
Keyed on agent_type because the PreToolUse payload carries agent_type and
no teammate name. Use the UNNAMESPACED type ('test-writer'), which is what
the hook receives — not the 'agent-team:test-writer' form that config.json
records.
Globs are matched against paths relative to the project root. Supported:
'*' (one segment), '**' (any depth), '?' (one character). A leading '!'
excludes. A path matches when it hits at least one non-'!' glob and no '!'
glob. Negation always wins — there is no last-match-wins precedence — so
entries are written to be disjoint rather than layered.
An agent type with no entry here is UNCONSTRAINED. Keep each entry in step
with the matching agents/<role>.md — a map narrower than the definition
denies writes the role was explicitly told it owns.
test-writer and test-infra are deliberately disjoint. test-writer owns test
files; test-infra owns everything that makes them runnable. The negations on
test-writer hand the shared machinery to test-infra, and the '!**/tsconfig*'
entry exists because 'tsconfig.test.json' matches '**/*.test.*' by accident —
a TypeScript compiler config is not a test file.
EVERY role carries '!.claude/**', and any role added later must too. That
directory holds the machinery that governs the agents themselves — this
ownership map, the agent definitions, settings, and the configuration of
whatever hooks a project has installed. Enforcement an agent can rewrite is
not enforcement: a role able to edit its own map grants itself any path, and
a role able to edit a quality gate's command config can neuter the gate
silently, leaving no failure behind to report. Changing anything under
.claude/ is a human decision, like the root tsconfig.json.
